en: The Two Matrices:
The Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Text—
Preliminaries
The preliminary duties are:
the broom, the lamp, water, and the seat;
these are called the "preliminary duties" for the Uposatha.
The prior duties are:
the motion (chanda), purity (pārisuddhi), the announcement of the season (utukkhaṇa), the counting of the number of bhikkhunīs, and the exhortation (ovāda).
These are called the "prior duties" of the Uposatha.
The Uposatha is performed with the entire assembly present, as many bhikkhunīs as are competent for the formal act are present,
and no common offenses exist.
And since there are no persons to be excluded from that assembly, it is said to be "fitting" (*pattakalla*).

Having completed the preliminary tasks and duties, we perform the act of honoring by reciting the Pātimokkha with the consent of the harmonious Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs who have confessed their offenses. The Recitation of the Introduction.
Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
Today is the Uposatha of the fifteenth day.
If it is agreeable to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha.
What is the preliminary duty of the Saṅgha?
Venerable ladies, announce your purity;
I shall recite the Pātimokkha.
Let all of us together listen well and attend closely.
Whoever has committed an offense should disclose it;
one who has no offense should remain silent.
"Venerable ladies, by your silence, I shall understand that you are pure.
Just as there is an individual response when one is questioned separately, so too is it declared a third time for an assembly such as this.
Any bhikkhunī who, when it has been announced a third time, does not disclose an existing offense while being mindful, commits an intentional falsehood."
Furthermore, venerable ladies, intentional lying has been called an obstructive state by the Blessed One.
Therefore, a bhikkhunī who remembers having committed an offense and desires purification must disclose that offense;
for once it is disclosed, she will find ease.
Noble ladies, the introduction has been recited.
Therefore, I ask you, noble ladies: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
You are pure here, venerable sirs; therefore, by your silence, I shall so hold it.
The Introduction is concluded.
The Exposition of the Pārājikas:
Herein, these eight pārājika rules come up for recitation.
Pārājika 1: The Training Rule on Sexual Intercourse.
Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should intentionally engage in sexual intercourse, even with an animal, she is defeated and no longer in communion.
Pārājika 2: The Training Rule on Taking What Is Not Given.
Whichever bhikkhunī, whether from a village or from a forest, should take what is not given, constituting theft—

In whatever kind of taking what is not given kings, having seized a thief, would execute him, imprison him, or banish him, saying, "You are a thief! You are a fool! You are deluded! You are a robber!", if a bhikkhunī takes such an object that is not given, she too is defeated and no longer in communion.
Pārājika 3: The Training Rule on Sexual Intercourse with Humans.
Whatever nun should intentionally deprive a human being of life, or seek a weapon for him, or praise the beauty of death, or incite him to death, saying:
"O man, what is the use of this wretched, miserable life to you?

Death is better for you than life," thus with a mind desiring his death and an intention desiring his death, in many ways praising the beauty of death or inciting him to death—[this is a pārājika offense].
This too is an offense entailing defeat;
she is no longer in communion. Pārājika 4:

The Training Rule on Superhuman Qualities Whatever nun, without direct knowledge, should claim for herself a superhuman quality—a noble state of knowledge and vision worthy of the Ariyans—saying, "Thus I know, thus I see," [is defeated].

Then, at a later time, whether being examined or not being examined, if she—having committed an offense and desiring purification—should say, "Venerable lady, I said I knew when I did not know; I said I saw when I did not see;
I spoke empty falsehood," except through overweening pride, she too is defeated and no longer in communion.
Pārājika 5. The Training Rule on Touching Above the Knees.
Whatever nun, being lustful, should consent to being touched, stroked, grasped, contacted, or pressed against below the collarbone and above the knees by a lustful man—this too [is a pārājika].
She is one who has committed a *pārājika* offense and is no longer in communion, having [acted] above the kneecaps. *Pārājika* 6: The Training Rule on Concealing Faults.
Whatever nun, knowing that another nun has committed a *pārājika* offense, neither herself admonish her, nor...
If she does not inform the Saṅgha, and when that nun has either passed away, been expelled, or left the order,
she later says: "Venerable ladies, I already knew of this nun that 'this sister is such and such,' yet I did not reproach her myself nor inform the Saṅgha"— this too is a Pārājika offense.
She is one who is not in communion, a concealer of faults.
Pārājika 7: The Training Rule on Following One Who Has Been Suspended.
Whatever nun, however, follows a monk who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—

If she should continue to follow that monk who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha—suspended in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction—for being disrespectful, unrepentant, and for not making amends, that bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:

“Venerable lady, this monk has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction, for being disrespectful, unrepentant, and for not making amends; do not, venerable lady, follow this monk.

If, even when addressed by the bhikkhunīs in this way, that bhikkhunī should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that course of action.
If, being exhorted up to the third time, she should relinquish that, it is well;
if she should not relinquish it, she too is one who has committed a *pārājika* offense, one who is no longer in communion, one who follows the suspended nun.
*Pārājika* 8: The Training Rule on the Eight Points.
Whatever nun, being lustful, should consent to taking hold of the hand of a lustful man,
or consent to taking hold of the corner of his outer robe, or should stand together with him, or converse with him, or go to a rendezvous,
or consent to a man coming to her, or enter a concealed place, or expose her body for that purpose— [this is an offense entailing suspension].
If she should provide [anything] for the purpose of indulging in this unrighteous practice, she too is defeated and excluded from the community;
this constitutes one of the eight grounds. Noble ladies, the eight rules involving defeat have been recited.
Having committed any one or another of these, a bhikkhunī does not obtain communion with the bhikkhunīs.
As it was before, so it is after; she is one who has committed a *pārājika* offense and is no longer in communion.
Therefore, I ask the noble ladies: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
The Venerable Ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The section on the *pārājika* offenses is concluded.
The Exposition of the Saṅghādisesa Rules.
Venerable ladies, these seventeen Saṅghādisesa rules come up for recitation.
Saṅghādisesa 1: The Training Rule on Litigiousness.
Whatever bhikkhunī should live as a litigant with a householder, a householder’s son, a slave, a laborer,
or even with a wandering ascetic or a paribbājaka— this bhikkhunī too has committed an offense that entails immediate defeat, a *saṅghādisesa* offense involving banishment.
Saṅghādisesa 2: The Training Rule on Ordaining a Female Thief.

Whatever bhikkhunī, knowing that a woman is a thief condemned to death and having been identified, should ordain her without having obtained permission from the king, or the Saṅgha, or a group, or a guild, or a clan—unless it is a legal exemption—this bhikkhunī also incurs an offense entailing immediate confession (paṭhamāpattika).
[This is] a Dhamma that has been committed, which entails expulsion and is a *saṅghādisesa*.
*Saṅghādisesa* 3: The Training Rule on Going to Another Village Alone.
Whatever bhikkhunī should go to another village alone, or should go to the other side of a river alone, or [should go alone...]

If she should spend the night apart [from her community], or if she should be left behind by the group alone, this nun too has committed an offense that is an immediate transgression, a *saṅghādisesa*, which entails being sent away.
*Saṅghādisesa* 4: The training rule on reintegrating one who has been suspended.
Whatever nun, however, should restore a nun who has been suspended by a unanimous Saṅgha in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction,
without having obtained the consent of the Saṅgha that performed the act and without knowing the will of the assembly—
this nun also has committed an offense that is an immediate offense, a *saṅghādisesa*, involving expulsion.
Saṅghādisesa 5. The First Training Rule on Receiving Food.

Whatever bhikkhunī, being lustful, having with her own hand received from the hand of a lustful man either solid food or soft food, should chew it or eat it—this bhikkhunī also commits an offense entailing immediate confession.
An offense entailing the Dhamma, leading to expulsion, a *saṅghādisesa*.
**Saṅghādisesa 6: The Second Training Rule on Receiving Food** Whichever bhikkhunī should speak thus: “What can this man do for you, Noble Lady? He is lustful...”
Or, if she is not free from lust, saying: "Since you are free from lust, come, noble lady,
having received with your own hand whatever hard food or soft food this man gives you, eat it or consume it"—
this nun too has committed an offense that is an immediate transgression, a *saṅghādisesa*, which entails being sent away from the community.

Saṅghādisesa 7: The Training Rule on Meddling in Marital Affairs Whatever bhikkhunī should engage in meddling in marital affairs— either conveying a man’s intent to a woman, or a woman’s intent to a man,
whether for the state of a husband or for the state of a lover, even if only for a moment— that bhikkhunī has committed an offense entailing immediate confession (paṭhamāpattika).
[They have] fallen into an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which entails expulsion from the Dhamma. **Saṅghādisesa 8:

The Training Rule on Malice** Whatever nun, out of malice, hatred, or ill-will, should groundlessly accuse another nun of an offense entailing defeat (*pārājika*), thinking, "Perhaps I might cause her to fall away from this holy life," [commits a *saṅghādisesa*].
Then, at a later time, whether being interrogated or not being interrogated,
if that legal issue is found to be groundless and the nun persists in her accusation,
this nun also has committed an offense that is an immediate transgression, a *saṅghādisesa* involving expulsion.
Saṅghādisesa 9: The Training Rule on Matters Belonging to Another Case Whichever bhikkhunī,
being angry, ill-willed, and displeased with another bhikkhunī, should, on account of some slight matter or mere pretext belonging to a legal issue of a different category,
accuse her of an offense entailing defeat (*pārājika*), thinking, "Perhaps I might cause her to fall away from this holy life," [she commits a saṅghādisesa].
Then, at a later time, whether she is being interrogated or not, that legal issue turns out to be something of a different nature.
Only a slight portion, a mere trace, has been taken up, yet the nun maintains her position of fault.
This nun, too, has committed an offense that is an immediate transgression, a *saṅghādisesa* involving expulsion.
Saṅghādisesa 10: The Training Rule on Renouncing the Training Whatever bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should speak thus:
“I renounce the Buddha; I renounce the Dhamma; I renounce the Saṅgha; I renounce the training.”
“Why indeed should I practice the holy life only in the presence of those nuns who are daughters of the Sakyans?
There are other nuns who are modest, scrupulous, and desirous of training; in their presence I shall practice the holy life.
That nun should be addressed by the other nuns as follows:

“Noble lady, being angry and displeased, you spoke thus: ‘I renounce the Buddha, I renounce the Dhamma, I renounce the Saṅgha, I renounce the training; what indeed are these ascetics who are daughters of the Sakyans?
There are other ascetics who are modest, conscientious, and desirous of training—in their presence I shall lead the holy life.’”
‘I shall wander,’ [saying] ‘Delight, noble lady, the Dhamma is well-expounded; lead the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.

If that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [position].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, this nun also has committed an offense that is an offense entailing sending away (*saṅghādisesa*), which is to be dealt with up to the third time. **Saṅghādisesa 11:
The Training Rule on Being Angry over a Legal Matter** Whatever nun, being accused in some legal matter, being angry and displeased, should speak thus:
“If a nun says, ‘The nuns are led by desire; the nuns are led by hatred; the nuns are led by delusion; the nuns are led by fear,’ that nun should be addressed by the other nuns thus:
‘Venerable lady, do not, when you have been rebuked in some legal matter and are angry and displeased, speak thus:
“The nuns are led by desire; the nuns are led by hatred; the nuns are led by delusion; the nuns are led by fear.”’”
“...and the nuns,” [she says], “the noble lady might go out of favoritism, she might go out of ill-will, she might go out of delusion,
or she might go out of fear. If that nun,
being thus addressed by the nuns, should persist in her position as before, that nun is to be formally admonished by the nuns up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that course.
If, being exhorted up to three times, she should relinquish it, that is well;
if she does not relinquish it, this nun too has committed an offense entailing a third admonition, a *saṅghādisesa* offense which entails formal meeting and banishment.
*Saṅghādisesa* 12: The First Training Rule on Evil Conduct.
Now, if bhikkhunīs live in close association, behaving badly, having a bad reputation, being of evil notoriety, harassing the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and concealing each other’s faults,
those bhikkhunīs should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Sisters, you are living in close association, behaving badly, having a bad reputation, being of evil notoriety, harassing the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and concealing each other’s faults.”
“Live secluded, venerable ladies; the Saṅgha praises seclusion for sisters.
If those nuns, being thus addressed by the nuns, should persist as before, those nuns are to be formally admonished up to three times by the nuns for the sake of relinquishing that [behavior].
If, being admonished up to three times, they relinquish it, that is good.
If they do not desist, these bhikkhunīs too have committed an offense that is an offense involving defeat after the third [admonition], which entails expulsion, a *saṅghādisesa*.
*Saṅghādisesa* 13: The Second Training Rule on Evil Conduct.
Whichever bhikkhunī should speak thus:
“Venerable ladies, you should indeed live together; do not live apart.
There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such reputation, and such fame, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults, yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.
But to you alone the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, gossiping, and weakness: ‘Sisters...’”
“They live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame, harassers of the community of bhikkhunīs, and concealers of each other’s faults;
‘Withdraw, noble ladies! The Saṅgha of sisters praises seclusion alone.
That bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Noble lady, do not speak thus.
Noble lady, you two should live in association; do not live apart.

There are other bhikkhunīs in the Saṅgha who are of such conduct, such speech, and such behavior, who harass the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and conceal each other’s faults, yet the Saṅgha says nothing to them.”
"It is you yourselves whom the Saṅgha speaks thus out of contempt, disdain, impatience, talkativeness, and weakness:
'Sisters, you live in close association, of evil conduct, of evil reputation, of evil fame, harassers of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha, and concealers of each other's faults;
separate yourselves, noble ladies! The Saṅgha praises seclusion for the sisters.'"
And if that nun, being thus addressed by the nuns, should persist as before, that nun is to be formally admonished by the nuns up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that course.
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is well;
but if she does not relinquish it, this nun also has committed an offense that is to be dealt with at the third admonition, a *saṅghādisesa* offense involving expulsion.

Saṅghādisesa 14: The Training Rule on Causing a Schism in the Saṅgha Whatever bhikkhunī should strive for a schism in a harmonious Saṅgha, or should persist in taking up and maintaining a legal issue conducive to a schism—she should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Venerable lady, do not strive for a schism in a harmonious Saṅgha, nor persist in taking up and maintaining a legal issue conducive to a schism.”
“Friend, come together with the Saṅgha; for when the Saṅgha is united, living in harmony, without dispute, and following a single recitation, it dwells in comfort.

If that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [position].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, this nun too has committed an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa), which involves being sent away, after a third admonition.
Saṅghādisesa 15: The Training Rule on Following Those Who Cause Schism.
Now, there may be one, two, or three nuns who follow that very nun and speak divisively; they might say this:
“Venerable ladies, do not say anything at all to this bhikkhunī;

this bhikkhunī speaks according to the Dhamma, this bhikkhunī speaks according to the Vinaya, and this bhikkhunī speaks having taken up our own will and preference. She knows but does not speak; this is acceptable to us.”
Those bhikkhunīs should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
"Venerable ladies, do not speak in this way;
for this bhikkhunī does not speak according to the Dhamma, nor does this bhikkhunī speak according to the Vinaya."
"Venerable ladies, even the schism of the Saṅgha was not pleasing to you;
it would be better for you to be reconciled with the Saṅgha, for the Saṅgha, being united, in harmony, without dispute, and following a single recitation, dwells in comfort.

If those bhikkhunīs, when addressed thus by the bhikkhunīs, should still persist as before, those bhikkhunīs are to be formally admonished up to three times by the bhikkhunīs for the sake of relinquishing that position.
If, being exhorted up to the third time, they should relinquish it, that is well.
If they do not relinquish it, these bhikkhunīs too have committed an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa), which involves expulsion, after the third [exhortation].
Saṅghādisesa 16: The Training Rule on Being Difficult to Correct.

Now, if a bhikkhunī is of a contentious nature and, when being addressed by the bhikkhunīs in accordance with the Dhamma regarding the training rules included in the recitation, makes herself unaddressable, saying:
"Do not say anything to me, noble ladies, whether good or bad; nor will I say anything to you, noble ladies, whether good or bad;
desist, noble ladies, from speaking to me."
That bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
“Venerable lady, do not make yourself unadmonishable; let the venerable lady make herself admonishable.
Let the venerable lady speak to the bhikkhunīs in accordance with the Dhamma, and the bhikkhunīs will also speak to the venerable lady in accordance with the Dhamma.”
"For the assembly of that Blessed One is thus developed through mutual exhortation and mutual encouragement.

If, being spoken to by the bhikkhunīs in this way, that bhikkhunī should still persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [position].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, this nun too has committed an offense that is a *saṅghādisesa*, which involves formal meeting of the Saṅgha and entails expulsion, occurring upon the third admonition.
*Saṅghādisesa* 17: The Training Rule on Corrupting Families.
Now, if a nun dwells in dependence upon a certain village or town, being a corrupter of families and of evil conduct;
Her evil conduct is both seen and heard, and families corrupted by her are both seen and heard.
That bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus:
"Venerable lady, you are a corrupter of families and of evil conduct; indeed, your evil conduct is both seen and heard."
“Moreover, noble lady, families corrupted by you are seen and heard of; depart from this residence, noble lady, enough of your staying here.
If that bhikkhunī, being spoken to thus by the bhikkhunīs, should say to those bhikkhunīs:
“If there are bhikkhunīs who proceed out of favoritism, bhikkhunīs who proceed out of ill will, bhikkhunīs who proceed out of delusion,
and bhikkhunīs who proceed out of fear, and they grant probation to some for such an offense while not granting it to others,” that bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs as follows:
“Noble lady, do not speak thus. The bhikkhunīs are not swayed by favoritism, nor are they swayed by ill will, nor are they swayed by delusion, nor are they swayed by fear.

It is you, noble lady, who are a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Your evil conduct is both seen and heard, and families corrupted by you are both seen and heard. Depart from this residence, noble lady!”
“Enough of your staying here!

If that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should still persist in that same way, she is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [behavior].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, this nun too has committed an offense that is an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), which involves being sent away after a third admonition.
Venerable ladies, the seventeen *saṅghādisesa* rules have been recited: nine that are offenses upon the first instance, and eight that are offenses after a third admonition.
Whichever of these a nun commits, that nun must undergo the period of penance (*mānatta*) for a fortnight before both Saṅghas.
A nun who has completed the *mānatta* penance should be rehabilitated wherever there is a community of twenty nuns.

If a community of nuns that is short of even one member of the group of twenty should rehabilitate that nun, she is not rehabilitated and those nuns are to be censured; this is the proper procedure in such a case.
Herein, noble ladies, I ask you: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
You are pure in this matter, friends, therefore you are silent; thus do I understand it.
The Saṅghādisesas are finished.
Now, venerable ladies, these thirty Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules come up for recitation.
The Chapter on Bowls.
The Offense of Expiation involving Forfeiture 1. The Training Rule on the Accumulation of Almsbowls:
Whatever bhikkhunī should accumulate almsbowls, there is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture.

Nissaggiya Pācittiya 2: The Training Rule on Receiving Out-of-Season Robe-Cloth Whichever bhikkhunī, having determined an out-of-season robe-cloth to be "seasonal robe-cloth," should cause it to be distributed, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya). Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3: The Training Rule on the Exchange of Robes-cloth Whichever bhikkhunī should exchange her own robe-cloth with that of another bhikkhunī, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
But if a nun, having exchanged a robe with another nun, should later say:
"Come, sister, here is your robe; bring back this robe for me; what is yours is yours alone, and what is mine is mine alone;
bring back this robe, give me back my own," and should either take it herself or cause it to be taken away—[this is an offense].
...or, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya). Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4:
The Training Rule on Requesting Something Else. Whatever nun, having requested one thing, should request something else, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.

Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5. The Training Rule on Exchanging One Thing for Another: Whichever bhikkhunī, having requested one thing, should request another thing, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6. The First Training Rule on Exchanging for What Belongs to the Saṅgha:

Whatever nun, however, should have another article exchanged for a requisite belonging to the Saṅgha that was intended for a specific purpose and designated for that purpose, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 7: The Second Training Rule on Exchanging for What Belongs to the Saṅgha.

Whatever nun, however, should have another article exchanged for a requisite belonging to the Saṅgha that was intended for a specific purpose, designated for that purpose, and requested [by her], it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8. The First Training Rule on Exchanging for a Group Purpose:
Whichever bhikkhunī should exchange, for some other purpose, a communal requisite intended for a specific purpose, there is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9. The Second Training Rule on Exchanging for a Group Purpose:

Whatever nun, however, should cause something else to be procured by means of a requisite intended for another purpose, designated for another, belonging to a group, and obtained through solicitation, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*).
The Tenth Training Rule on Procuring for an Individual:

Whatever nun, however, should cause something else to be procured by means of a requisite intended for another purpose, designated for another, belonging to an individual, and obtained through solicitation, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*).
The First Chapter on Robes.
The Chapter on Robes.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 11: The Training Rule on Heavy Cloaks.

When a nun is having a heavy cloak (*garupāvuraṇa*) made, it should be made at most four *kaṃsa* [in weight]. If she should have it made beyond that, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*).
12. The Training Rule on the Light Cloak (*lahupāvuraṇa-sikkhāpada*):

When a nun is having a light cloak (*lahupāvuraṇa*) made, it should be made at most two and a half *kaṃsa* [in weight]. If she should have it made beyond that, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 13: The Rule on the Kathina Cloth.
When a robe has been finished and the Kathina period has been removed, a bhikkhunī may keep an extra robe for a maximum of ten days.
For her who exceeds this limit, it is a Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 14. The Training Rule on Stored Garments (Udosita-sikkhāpada):

When a robe has been finished and the Kathina period has ended, if a bhikkhunī should be separated from her three robes for even one night, except by the formal authorization of the bhikkhunīs, it is a Nissaggiya Pācittiya offense.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 15. The Training Rule on Out-of-Season Robes (Akālacīvara-sikkhāpada):
When a robe has been finished for a bhikkhunī and the kaṭhina period has ended, if an out-of-season robe should accrue to that bhikkhunī, she may accept it if she so desires;
having accepted it, she must have it made up quickly.
If it is not sufficient, she may keep that robe for at most one month, provided there is hope for its completion.
If she should keep it beyond that time, even with the expectation of receiving more, it is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture. **Nissaggiya Pācittiya 16:

The Training Rule on Requesting from an Unfamiliar Person** Whatever nun should request a robe from an unrelated householder or housewife, except at the proper occasion, it is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture.
In this regard, the appropriate occasion is when a bhikkhunī’s robe has been stolen or her robe has been lost;
this is the occasion there. Nissaggiya Pācittiya 17:
The Training Rule on Excess If an unrelated householder or housewife should invite a bhikkhunī to accept many robes, that bhikkhunī may accept no more than an inner and an outer robe from them.
If she should accept it beyond that, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 18: The First Rule on What Has Been Set Aside.
Now, if a robe-fund has been set aside for a bhikkhunī by an unrelated householder or housewife, [thinking]: "With this robe-fund, let such-and-such a robe be purchased and given to that bhikkhunī."
“Having purchased a robe with this robe-fund, I shall clothe the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with a robe.
If that bhikkhunī, not having been previously invited, should approach him and make a specification regarding the robe, saying:
“It would be good indeed if the venerable one, having purchased such and such a robe with this robe-fund, would clothe me with it,” [she commits an offense].
Out of a desire for something beautiful, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya). Nissaggiya Pācittiya 19:

The Second Training Rule on What Has Been Set Aside If, with reference to a bhikkhunī, separate funds for robes have been set aside by two unrelated householders or householders’ wives, [thinking]: “Let us each provide a robe for this bhikkhunī.”
“Having purchased separate robes with these funds for purchasing separate robes, we shall clothe the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with robes.
Now, if that bhikkhunī, not having been previously invited, should approach them and make a specification regarding the robes, saying:

“It would be good, venerable sirs, if you were to purchase such and such a robe or such and such a robe with these funds for purchasing separate robes and clothe me; both of you together with one [robe],” [she commits an offense].
Out of a desire for what is wholesome, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 20: The Training Rule on Kings.
Should a king, a royal official, a brahmin, or a householder, having sent a messenger with cloth-funds intended for a specific bhikkhunī, say: [text continues]
“Having purchased cloth with this money for robe-material, clothe the bhikkhunī named so-and-so with the robe.
If that messenger, having approached that bhikkhunī, should speak thus:
“Venerable lady, this money for robe-material has been brought for the sake of the venerable one; may the venerable one accept the money for robe-material.”
That nun should say this to the messenger:
"Friend, we do not accept robe-funds; rather, we accept robes at the proper time, provided they are allowable.
If that messenger should say this to that nun:
“If there is anyone who can act as an attendant for you,
noble lady?”— for a bhikkhunī who needs robes, monks, an attendant should be pointed out, whether he be an āraññika or an upāsaka,
saying: “This one, friends, is an attendant for the bhikkhunīs.”
If the messenger, having informed that attendant, should approach that bhikkhunī and say:
"Venerable lady, the person whom the noble lady designated as her attendant has been informed by me; please approach him at the proper time, and he will clothe you with the robe-cloth.
Then, monks, the attendant should approach the bhikkhunī who needs a robe and should be urged and reminded two or three times:
“If [the donor says], ‘I need a robe,
friend,’ and after being urged and reminded two or three times, he produces that robe, it is good;
if he does not produce it, she should stand silently for his sake up to four, five, or six times.”
If she should cause that robe-cloth to be produced while standing silently in expectation for four, five, or at most six times, that is well.
But if, by striving beyond that, she should cause that robe-cloth to be produced, it is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture (*nissaggiya pācittiya*).
If she does not cause it to be produced, she must either go there herself or send a messenger to the place from which the robe-fund was brought, saying:
“Venerable sirs, that robe-fund which you have sent for the sake of a certain bhikkhunī does not serve any purpose for her. Venerable sirs, apply yourselves to your own affairs;
let not your own property go to waste.
This is the proper course in such a case.
The second chapter on robes.
The chapter on bowls.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21: The training rule on money.
Whatever nun should acquire gold or silver, or cause it to be acquired, or consent to its being deposited for her, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).

Nissaggiya Pācittiya 22: The Training Rule on Trading in Money Whatever nun should engage in various kinds of trading in money, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 23. The Training Rule on Buying and Selling:
Whatever nun should engage in various kinds of buying and selling, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 24. The Training Rule on Less than Five Bindings: [Whatever nun should have a robe made that is less than five spans in width...]
Whatever nun, however, should have another new bowl made when her own bowl has less than five mends, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya-pācittiya).
That nun must relinquish that bowl to the assembly of nuns;
and whatever is the least bowl among that assembly of nuns, that must be given back to that nun.
“This alms-bowl is yours; it is to be kept until it breaks”—this is the proper course in this matter.
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25: The Training Rule on Medicines.
Now, those medicines that are to be taken internally by sick bhikkhunīs, such as:
Ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses: having accepted these, they may be used after being stored for a maximum of seven days.
For one who exceeds that limit, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya). Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26: The Training Rule on Taking Away Robes.

Whatever nun, having herself given a robe to another nun, being angry and displeased, should take it back or cause it to be taken back, commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 27: The Training Rule on Requesting Thread.
Whatever nun, having herself requested thread, should have a robe woven by weavers, commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).

Nissaggiya Pācittiya 28: The Training Rule on the Great Weavers If an unrelated householder or housewife should have a robe woven by weavers for the sake of a nun, and if that nun, not having been previously invited, should approach those weavers and make a specification regarding the robe, saying:
"Friends, this robe is being woven for me; make it long, make it wide, make it thick, make it well-woven, make it well-spun, make it well-combed, and make it well-carded."
“Perhaps we too might give even a small thing to the Venerable Ones.
If that bhikkhunī, having spoken thus, should give even a small thing, even as much as a mere alms-food gift, it is an offense of expiation involving forfeiture (nissaggiya pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 29: The Training Rule on Urgent Robes (Accekacīvara-sikkhāpada)
If, ten days before the full moon of the month of Kattika, a robe intended as a gift for a bhikkhunī should arise, that bhikkhunī, considering it urgent, may accept it;
having accepted it, she may keep it until the time for robes.
If she should keep it beyond that, it is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya-pācittiya).
Nissaggiya Pācittiya 30. The Training Rule on What Has Been Designated.
Whatever nun, knowing that a gain intended for the Saṅgha has been designated, should herself appropriate it, incurs an offense entailing relinquishment and confession (nissaggiya pācittiya).
The third section: The Chapter on Alms Bowls.
Ladies, the thirty rules on offenses entailing relinquishment and confession have been recited.
Therefore, ladies, I ask you: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
The Venerable Ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The rules on offenses entailing relinquishment and confession (Nissaggiya-Pācittiya) are concluded.
Pure Pācittiyas:
Now, venerable ladies, these one hundred and sixty-six rules of Pācittiya come up for recitation.
The Garlic Chapter.
Pācittiya 1. The Training Rule on Garlic:
Whatever bhikkhunī should eat garlic, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 2.
The Training Rule on Pubic Hair: [Whatever bhikkhunī should have the hair of her private parts removed... [text fragment]
Whatever nun should have hair removed from the private parts, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 3: The Training Rule on Slapping with the Palm. In the case of slapping with the palm, it is an offense entailing expiation.
Pācittiya 4. The Training Rule on Salve-Sticks:
It is an offense of expiation for [using] a salve-stick. Pācittiya 5.
The Training Rule on Purification by Water: [It is an offense of expiation for using water for purification.]
When a nun takes water for washing, she must take no more than two finger-joints' worth.
For one who exceeds that limit, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 6:
The Training Rule on Attending Upon Whichever nun, however, attends upon a monk while he is eating by providing him with drinking water or a fan, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 7. The Training Rule on Raw Grain.

Whatever bhikkhunī, having requested raw grain, or having had it requested, or having roasted it, or having had it roasted, or having pounded it, or having had it pounded, or having cooked it, or having had it cooked, should eat it, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 8. The First Training Rule on Disposal of Excrement.
Whatever nun should discard or cause to be discarded excrement, urine, rubbish, or food scraps over a wall or over a fence, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 9: The Second Training Rule on Discarding Excrement Whatever nun should discard or cause to be discarded excrement, urine, rubbish, or food scraps upon green crops, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 10. The Training Rule on Dancing, Singing, and Music.
Whatever bhikkhunī should go to see dancing, singing, or instrumental music, there is an offense of expiation.
The first section, on garlic, is concluded.
The Chapter on Darkness at Night.
Pācittiya 11: The Training Rule on Darkness at Night.
Whatever nun, in darkness at night and without a lamp, should stand or converse alone with a man, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 12. The Training Rule on a Concealed Place:
Whichever bhikkhunī, in a concealed place, should stand or converse alone with a man, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 13. The Training Rule on Conversing Outdoors:
Whatever nun, however, should stand or converse alone with a man in the open air, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 14:

The Training Rule on Sending Away a Companion Whatever nun, however, should stand or converse alone with a man on a carriage road, in a cul-de-sac, or at a crossroads; or should whisper into his ear, or send away her companion nun—it is an offense entailing expiation.

Pācittiya 15. The Training Rule on Departing Without Asking Permission Whichever bhikkhunī, having approached families before the meal and sat down on a seat, should depart without asking permission of the owners, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 16. The Training Rule on Sitting Down Without Asking Permission Whichever bhikkhunī, having approached families before the meal and sat down on a seat, should sit down again without asking permission of the owners, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whatever nun, having approached families after the meal, should sit down or lie down on a seat without having asked the owner’s permission, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 17: The Training Rule on Spreading Out Without Permission.

Whatever nun, having approached families at an improper time, should spread out a bed or have one spread out, and then sit down or lie down upon it without having asked the owner’s permission, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 18. The Training Rule on Causing Another to Be Reprimanded:
Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should cause another to be reprimanded based on what is wrongly grasped or wrongly understood, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 19. The Training Rule on Swearing at Another:
Whatever bhikkhunī should curse herself or another with reference to hell or the holy life, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 20: The Training Rule on Weeping Whatever bhikkhunī should weep, striking herself again and again, it is an offense entailing confession.
The second chapter: The Section on Darkness at Night.
The Section on Nakedness.
Pācittiya 21: The Training Rule on Being Naked.
Whatever nun should bathe naked, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 22: The Training Rule on the Bathing Cloak.
Now, when a nun is having a bathing cloak made, it must be made according to the proper measure; this is the measure: [text follows].
It is four spans long according to the Sugata-span and two spans wide. For one who exceeds these measurements, there is an offense of expiation involving cutting.
Pācittiya 23: The Training Rule on Sewing Robes.

Whatever nun, having had another nun’s robe unsewn or having had it unsewn by someone else, subsequently, while there is no obstacle, neither sews it herself nor makes an effort to have it sewn, except within four or five days, commits a *pācittiya*.
*Pācittiya* 24. The Training Rule on the Movement of the Outer Robe (*Saṅghāṭicāra*).
Whatever nun should exceed the five-day limit for the movement of the outer robe, commits a *pācittiya*.
Pācittiya 25. The Training Rule on the Exchange of Robes:

Whatever bhikkhunī should wear a robe intended for exchange, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 26. The Training Rule on Group Robes: Whatever bhikkhunī should accept a group robe [intended for a specific individual], there is an offense of expiation.
Whatever nun should create an obstacle to the community’s acquisition of robe-cloth, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 27: The Training Rule on Obstructing Whatever nun should obstruct a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 28. The Training Rule on Giving Robes.
Whichever bhikkhunī should give a robe belonging to a recluse to a householder, or to a male wanderer, or to a female wanderer, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 29. The Training Rule on Exceeding the Time Limit.
Whatever nun, however, should let the period for making robes pass by when there is only a weak expectation of obtaining robe-cloth, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 30: The Training Rule on the Suspension of the Kathina.
Whatever nun, however, should obstruct a legitimate suspension of the Kathina, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
The Third Chapter on the Naked.
The Chapter on Tuvaṭṭa.
Pācittiya 31: The Training Rule on Sitting on the Same Bed.
If any two nuns should lie down on the same bed, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 32: The Training Rule on Lying Down with a Single Covering.
If any two nuns should lie down under one covering and one upper garment, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 33. The Training Rule on Causing Discomfort:
Whatever bhikkhunī should intentionally cause discomfort to another bhikkhunī, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 34. The Training Rule on Not Attending:
Whatever bhikkhunī, however, does not nurse a co-resident who is suffering, nor makes an effort to have her nursed, commits a pācittiya offense.

Pācittiya 35: The Training Rule on Expelling Whatever bhikkhunī, having given a dwelling place to another bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should herself expel her or cause her to be expelled, commits a pācittiya offense.
Pācittiya 36. The Training Rule on Intimacy (Saṃsaṭṭha-sikkhāpada).
Whichever nun should live in intimacy with a householder or a householder’s son, that nun should be addressed by the nuns thus:
“Venerable lady, do not live in intimacy with a householder or a householder’s son; separate yourself, venerable lady, for seclusion alone is praised by the Sangha for a sister.”

And if that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [behavior].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 37. The Training Rule on Within One’s Own Country:

Should any bhikkhunī travel on a journey within her own country when it is considered dangerous and risky, and she is without a caravan, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya). Pācittiya 38. The Training Rule on Beyond One’s Own Country: [Should any bhikkhunī travel on a journey beyond her own country when it is considered dangerous and risky, and she is without a caravan, she commits an offense entailing confession.]
Whatever bhikkhunī should travel on a journey through foreign countries that are considered dangerous and perilous without a caravan, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 39: The Training Rule on During the Rains Retreat.
Whatever bhikkhunī should go on a journey during the rains retreat, there is an offense entailing expiation.
Pācittiya 40. The Training Rule on Setting Out on a Wanderer’s Tour.
Whichever nun, having completed the rains residence, does not set out on a wanderer’s tour—even if only for five or six *yojanas*—commits a Pācittiya offense.
The fourth section, the Chapter on Hastening.
The Chapter on Painted Halls.
Pacittiya 41: The Training Rule on Royal Palaces.
Whatever bhikkhunī should go to see a royal palace, a painted hall, a monastery, a pleasure grove, or a lotus pond, it is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 42. The Training Rule on Using High Seats or Couches:
Whichever bhikkhunī should use a high seat or a couch, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 43. The Training Rule on Spinning Thread:
Whichever bhikkhunī should spin thread, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 44: The Training Rule on Lay Service.
Whichever bhikkhunī should perform lay service, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 45: The Training Rule on Legal Matters Whichever bhikkhunī,
when addressed by another bhikkhunī, “Come, noble lady, settle this legal matter,” and having promised,
“Very well,” subsequently fails to settle it— provided there is no obstacle— and makes no effort to settle it, [commits an offense].
If she should do so, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 46:

The Training Rule on Giving Food Whichever bhikkhunī should, with her own hand, give fresh or cooked food to a householder, or to a male wanderer, or to a female wanderer—it is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 47. The Training Rule on Lodging Robes:

Whatever bhikkhunī should use a lodging robe without having relinquished it, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 48. The Training Rule on Lodgings and Monasteries: [Whatever bhikkhunī should appropriate a lodging or a monastery belonging to the Saṅgha for her own personal use, there is an offense of expiation.]
Whatever nun, however, should set out on a journey without having assigned her lodging, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 49: The Training Rule on the Study of Animal Sciences.
Whatever nun, however, should study animal sciences, it is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 50. The Training Rule on Teaching Secular Arts.
Whatever bhikkhunī should teach secular arts, there is an offense of expiation.
The fifth section, the Chapter on Picture Galleries.
The Chapter on Parks.
Pācittiya 51: The Training Rule on Entering a Park.
Whatever nun, knowing that a park has monks in it, should enter it without having asked permission, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 52. The Training Rule on Abusing a Monk:
Should any bhikkhunī abuse or revile a bhikkhu, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 53. The Training Rule on Reviling a Group: [Should any bhikkhunī revile a group, it is an offense of expiation.]
Whichever bhikkhunī, being angry, should revile a group, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 54: The Training Rule on Being Invited.
Whichever bhikkhunī, having been invited or having already finished her meal, should eat or consume either solid food or soft food, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 55. The Training Rule on Being Stingy with Families:

Whatever bhikkhunī should be stingy with families, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 56. The Training Rule on a Residence Without Bhikkhus: [Whatever bhikkhunī should reside in a residence where no bhikkhus are present, there is an offense of expiation.]
If a bhikkhunī should spend the rains residence in a dwelling where no bhikkhus are present, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 57: The Training Rule on Not Inviting Criticism If a bhikkhunī, having completed the rains residence, does not invite criticism from both Saṅghas regarding three matters—namely, what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected—it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 58. The Training Rule on Exhortation:
Whichever bhikkhunī does not go for the purpose of exhortation or for communal living incurs an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 59. The Training Rule on Approaching for Exhortation:

Every half-month, two things should be expected from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus by a bhikkhunī: the inquiry regarding the Uposatha and the approaching for the exhortation. For one who lets this pass, there is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 60: The Training Rule on What is Born in the Groin.
Whichever bhikkhunī, however, without having obtained permission from the Saṅgha or a group, [treats] a boil or a discharge born in the groin...
Or if she should have [the woman] separated from a man, or have her split apart, or have her washed, or have her anointed, or have her bound, or have her released,
it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
This is the sixth section, the Chapter on Monasteries (Ārāmavagga).
The Chapter on Pregnant Women, Pacittiya 61: The Training Rule on Pregnant Women.
Whichever bhikkhunī should ordain a pregnant woman, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 62. The Training Rule on Nursing Mothers:

Whatever nun should give the full admission to a nursing woman, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 63. The First Training Rule for a Trainee Nun: Whatever nun should give the full admission to a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules, there is an offense of expiation.
Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who has not trained for two years in the six rules, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
Pācittiya 64: The Second Rule on the *Sikkhamānā*.

Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who has trained for two years in the six rules but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
Pācittiya 65. The First Training Rule on Married Women:

Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a married woman who is less than twelve years old, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 66. The Second Training Rule on Married Women: [Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a married woman who is less than twelve years old, there is an offense of expiation.]

If any bhikkhunī should give the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 67: The Third Rule on Married Girls If any bhikkhunī should give the full admission to a married girl who is more than twelve years old and who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 68. The First Training Rule on Co-residents:
Whatever bhikkhunī, having given the full admission to a co-resident, neither herself supports her nor causes her to be supported for two years, incurs an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 69. The Training Rule on Not Following the Leader: [Whatever bhikkhunī does not follow the leader, incurs an offense of expiation.]
Whatever nun does not follow her preceptor for two years after she has been ordained, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 70: The Second Training Rule on Co-residents Whatever nun, having ordained a co-resident, neither sends her away nor causes her to be sent away—even if it is only five or six yojanas—there is an offense of expiation.
The Seventh Chapter on Pregnant Women.
The Chapter on Maidens.
Pācittiya 71: The First Training Rule Concerning Maidens.
Whatever nun should give the full admission to a maiden who is less than twenty years of age, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 72. The Second Training Rule on Maidens:
Whatever nun should give the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years of age, but who has not trained for two years in the six rules, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 73. The Third Training Rule on Maidens Should any bhikkhunī ordain a maiden who is twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been approved by the Saṅgha, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 74. The Training Rule on Being Less Than Twelve Years [of Standing]
Whatever nun, however, who is less than twelve years [of standing], should give the full admission, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 75: The Training Rule on Being Twelve Years of Standing Whatever nun, however, who is twelve years of standing but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, should give the full admission, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 76. The Training Rule on the Nature of Carping.
Whatever nun, when being told, “Enough, noble lady, of ordaining you for now,” should consent by saying, “Very well,” and later engage in the nature of carping, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 77. The First Training Rule on Ordaining a Trainee Nun.

If a nun, having said to a trainee nun, “Venerable lady, if you give me a robe, I will ordain you,” and subsequently, though there is no obstacle, neither ordains her nor makes an effort to have her ordained, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 78: The second training rule on not ordaining a trainee nun.
Whatever nun, having said to a trainee nun, "If you, noble lady, will follow me for two years,
then I will give you the full admission," should afterwards, while there is no obstacle, neither give her the full admission nor make an effort to have her admitted,
commits an offense entailing confession.
Pācittiya 79. The Training Rule on Dwelling in Sorrow:

Whichever bhikkhunī should give the full admission (*vuṭṭhāpanā*) to a trainee nun (*sikkhamānā*) who is associated with men, associated with boys, fierce, and dwelling in sorrow, there is an offense entailing expiation (*pācittiya*).
Pācittiya 80. The Training Rule on Not Being Authorized:

Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who has not been authorized by her mother and father or by her husband, there is an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*).

Pācittiya 81: The Training Rule on One Undergoing Probation Whichever bhikkhunī, however, should give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* through the giving of consent by one who is undergoing probation, there is an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*).
Pācittiya 82. The Training Rule on Every Year:

Whatever bhikkhunī should give the full admission every year, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 83. The Training Rule on One Year: [Whatever bhikkhunī should give the full admission to one who has been ordained for only one year, there is an offense of expiation.]
Whatever nun, however, should ordain two [nuns] in one year, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
The eighth section: The Chapter on Maidens.
The Chapter on Umbrellas and Footwear.
Pācittiya 84. The Training Rule on Umbrellas and Footwear:

Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should carry an umbrella and wear footwear, there is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 85. The Training Rule on Vehicles: [Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should ride in a vehicle, there is an offense of expiation.]
Whatever nun, not being ill, should travel by vehicle, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 86: The Training Rule on the Hip-Girdle Whatever nun should wear a hip-girdle (saṅghāṇi), it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 87. The Training Rule on Female Ornaments:
Should any bhikkhunī wear female ornaments, it is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 88. The Training Rule on Perfumes and Cosmetics:
Whatever nun should bathe with scents and ointments, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 89: The Training Rule on Perfumed Mustard Seed.
Whatever nun should bathe with perfumed mustard seed, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 90. The Training Rule on Having a Bhikkhunī Massaged.
Whatever bhikkhunī should have a bhikkhunī massaged or rubbed, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 91. The Training Rule on Having a Sikkhamānā Massaged.
Whatever bhikkhunī should have a female trainee (sikkhamānā) massage her or have her rub her body, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 92: The Training Rule on Having a Female Novice Massage One Whatever bhikkhunī should have a female novice (sāmaṇerī) massage her or have her rub her body, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 93. The Training Rule on Having a Laywoman Massage.
Whatever bhikkhunī should have a laywoman massage her or rub her body, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 94. The Training Rule on Not Informing. [Whatever bhikkhunī should go to see a man who is not related to her without informing him first... [text continues]
Whatever nun, however, should sit on a seat in front of a monk without having asked permission, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 95. The Training Rule on Asking Questions:
Whatever nun should ask a question of a monk who has not given her leave, it is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 96. The Training Rule on Not Wearing a Bodice.
Whatever bhikkhunī should enter a village without wearing a bodice, there is an offense of expiation.
The ninth section, on the Umbrella and Footwear.
The Chapter on False Speech.
Pācittiya 97: The Training Rule on False Speech.
In speaking a deliberate lie, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 98. The Training Rule on Slandering: In the case of slandering, it is an offense entailing expiation. Pācittiya 99. The Training Rule on Divisive Speech: [In the case of divisive speech, it is an offense entailing expiation.]
In the case of malicious talebearing among bhikkhunīs, there is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya). Pācittiya 100: The Training Rule on Reciting Word-by-Word.
Whatever bhikkhunī should cause one who is not fully ordained to recite the Dhamma word-by-word, there is an offense entailing confession.
Pācittiya 101. The First Training Rule on Sleeping Together.
Whatever bhikkhunī should share a sleeping place for more than two or three nights with one who is not fully ordained, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 102. The Second Training Rule on Sleeping Together.
Whichever bhikkhunī should lie down in the same bed with a man, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 103: The Training Rule on Teaching the Dhamma.
Whichever bhikkhunī should teach the Dhamma to a man in more than five or six sentences, except in the presence of a discerning woman, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 104. The Training Rule on Announcing Supernormal Attainments:

Should any bhikkhunī announce a superhuman state (uttarimanussadhamma) to one who is not fully ordained, if it be true, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 105. The Training Rule on Announcing Grave Matters: [Should any bhikkhunī announce a grave matter (duṭṭhulla) to one who is not fully ordained...]
Whatever nun should report a grave offense of another nun to one who is not fully ordained, except with the consent of the nuns, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 106: The Training Rule on Digging the Earth Whatever nun should dig the earth herself or cause it to be dug, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
The Tenth Chapter on False Speech.
The Chapter on Living Beings.
Pācittiya 107: The Training Rule on Living Beings.
Destruction of vegetation is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 108: The Training Rule on Speaking Otherwise.
Speaking otherwise or causing annoyance is an offense entailing expiation.
Pācittiya 109. The Training Rule on Rebuking:
In the case of rebuking or disparaging, it is a Pācittiya offense.
Pācittiya 110. The First Training Rule on Lodgings:
Whatever nun, having spread out or caused to be spread out in the open air a couch, a chair, a mattress, or a rug belonging to the Saṅgha,
departs without either putting it away herself or having it put away, or goes away without asking permission,
incurs an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 111. The Second Training Rule on Lodgings:

Whichever bhikkhunī, having spread out a bed or having had one spread out in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, departs without either putting it away herself or having it put away by another, or goes away without informing [another], commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 112. The Training Rule on Encroaching:
Whatever nun, in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, knowingly intrudes upon a nun who has already entered first and makes her bed there—
doing so solely for the purpose of thinking, “She will leave when she has need of space,” and for no other reason—
commits an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 113. The Training Rule on Expelling.
Whatever bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should expel or cause another to expel a bhikkhunī from a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 114. The Training Rule on the Gabled Upper Chamber.
Whatever nun, however, should sit down or lie down on a bed or bench with detachable legs in an upper chamber of a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 115: The Training Rule on Large Dwellings.

When a nun is having a large dwelling built for herself, she must determine the site while standing on ground that is not overgrown with vegetation, up to the door-posts, the installation of the bolt, the preparation of the window openings, and the allowance for two or three layers of roofing.
If she should resolve [to do so] while standing even further away than that, where there is no greenery, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 116: The Training Rule on Water Containing Living Beings.
Whatever nun, knowing that water contains living beings, should sprinkle grass or clay with it, or cause it to be sprinkled, commits an offense entailing expiation.
The Eleventh Chapter: On Villages of Spirits.
The Chapter on Food.
Pācittiya 117: The Training Rule on Alms from a Lodging House.
A sick nun may eat one meal at a public rest-house.
If she should eat more than that, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 118: The Training Rule on Eating in a Group.
Eating in a group, except on an appropriate occasion, is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).

Herein, this is the appropriate occasion: the occasion of illness, the occasion of the distribution of robes, the occasion of making robes, the occasion of traveling on a journey, the occasion of boarding a boat, the occasion of a great assembly, the occasion of a meal for recluses; this is the appropriate occasion therein.
Pācittiya 119: The Training Rule concerning Kāṇamātā.
If someone should invite a bhikkhunī who has entered a family with cakes or with flour-mash, the bhikkhunī, if she so desires, may accept two or three bowlfuls.
If she should accept more than that, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Having accepted two or three bowlfuls, she must then take them out and share them with the other bhikkhunīs; this is the proper course of action in such a case.
Pācittiya 120. The Training Rule on Eating at the Wrong Time:
Whichever bhikkhunī should chew or eat hard food or soft food at the wrong time, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 121. The Training Rule on Storing Food:
Whatever bhikkhunī should eat or consume fresh or cooked food that has been stored, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 122: The Training Rule on Tooth-sticks Whatever bhikkhunī should put into her mouth any food not given to her, except for water and tooth-sticks, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 123. The Training Rule on Sending Away.

Whichever bhikkhunī, having said to another bhikkhunī, "Come, noble lady, let us enter a village or town for alms," should then send her away—whether she has had food given to her or not—saying, "Go, noble lady; I have no conversation or sitting together with you."
“Or it is comfortable for me to speak or sit alone”—making this very reason and no other, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 124: The Training Rule on Eating with Others.
Whatever nun should sit down intruding upon a family where food is being served, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 125: The Training Rule on Secluded Places.
Whatever nun should sit down with a man in a secluded, concealed place, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 126. The Training Rule on Sitting in Secret.
Whatever bhikkhunī should sit in secret, one-on-one, with a man, there is an offense of expiation.
The twelfth section, on Eating.
The Chapter on Conduct.
Pācittiya 127. The Training Rule on Visiting.

Whatever bhikkhunī, having been invited with food, should visit families before or after the meal without having informed a bhikkhunī who is present, except on an appropriate occasion, commits a pācittiya offense.
In this regard, these are the exceptions: the time for giving robes and the time for making robes;
this is the exception here. Pācittiya 128: The Training Rule on Mahānāma.

A nun who is not ill may accept an invitation for requisites for four months, except for a renewed invitation and except for a permanent invitation. If she should accept it for longer than that, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 129. The Training Rule on Visiting an Arrayed Army:
Whichever bhikkhunī should go to see an arrayed army, except when there is a reason of such a kind, incurs a pācittiya offense.
Pācittiya 130. The Training Rule on Staying with an Army:

If there should arise some reason for that bhikkhunī to go to the army, she may stay with the army for two or three nights. If she should stay longer than that, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).

Pācittiya 131: The Training Rule on Military Displays If a bhikkhunī, while staying with an army for two or three nights, should go to see a military display, a review of troops, an array of the army, or a battle formation, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 132. The Training Rule on Drinking Intoxicants:
In drinking fermented liquor or spirits, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 133. The Training Rule on Tapping with Fingers: [In tapping another with the fingers, there is an offense of expiation.]
In tickling with the fingers, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 134: The Training Rule on Joking.
In joking about water, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 135. The Training Rule on Disrespect: In case of disrespect, it is an offense of expiation. Pācittiya 136.
The Training Rule on Terrifying: [In case of terrifying others, it is an offense of expiation.]
Whatever nun should frighten another nun, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
The thirteenth section on Conduct (Cāritta-vagga) is concluded. The section on Fire (Joti-vagga).
Pācittiya 137. The Training Rule on Fire:
Whatever nun, not being ill, should kindle a fire or have one kindled for the purpose of warming herself, except when there is a suitable reason, commits a pācittiya offense.
Pācittiya 138. The Training Rule on Bathing: [The rule concerning bathing follows.]
Whatever nun should bathe within half a month, except on the proper occasion, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).

Herein, this is the proper occasion: when there is "one and a half months remaining of the hot season," and the "first month of the rainy season"—these two and a half months are the time of heat, the time of feverish distress, the time of illness, the time of work, and the time of traveling on a journey.
This is the occasion for wind and rain; this is the exception in that regard.
Furthermore, whatever other novice monks obtain shared lodgings with bhikkhunīs for two or three nights—that too does not apply to you.
(Pācittiya 139: The Training Rule on Making [Robes] Discolored).
Furthermore, when a nun obtains a new robe, she must apply one of the three kinds of disfigurement:
either blue, mud-color, or dark brown. If a nun uses a new robe without applying one of these three kinds of disfigurement, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 140. The Training Rule on Assigning (Vikappana).

Whatever bhikkhunī, having herself assigned a robe to a bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female trainee, a male novice, or a female novice, should use it without having it formally relinquished, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 141. The Training Rule on Causing to Hide (Apanidhāpana).
Whatever nun should hide, or cause to be hidden, another nun’s bowl, robe, sitting mat, needle case, or waistband—even if only in jest—it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 142: The Training Rule on Intentional Killing Whatever nun should intentionally deprive a living being of life, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 143. The Training Rule on Water with Living Beings:
Should any bhikkhunī knowingly consume water containing living beings, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 144. The Training Rule on Reopening: [A bhikkhunī who reopens a settled legal issue] commits an offense entailing expiation.
Whatever nun, knowing that a legal issue has been settled in accordance with the Dhamma, should reopen it for a formal act, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 145: The Training Rule on Traveling with a Caravan of Thieves.

Whatever nun, knowing that she is traveling with a caravan of thieves, should set out together with them on a journey along a common road, even if only as far as the next village, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 146: The Training Rule on Ariṭṭha Whichever bhikkhunī should speak thus:

“As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called ‘obstructive states’ by the Blessed One are not sufficient to obstruct one who indulges in them,” [that bhikkhunī is to be dealt with according to the rule].
That bhikkhunī should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs thus: "Do not say so, Noble Lady;
do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One, for the Blessed One would not speak in such a way.
In many ways, Noble Lady, the obstructive states have been declared by the Blessed One to be obstructive, and they are sufficient to constitute an obstruction for one who indulges in them."

And if that bhikkhunī, being thus addressed by the bhikkhunīs, should persist as before, that bhikkhunī is to be formally admonished by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the sake of relinquishing that [behavior].
If, being admonished up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good.
If she does not relinquish it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
The Fourteenth Chapter: The Chapter on Views (Diṭṭhivagga). Pācittiya 147:
The Training Rule on Associating with One Who Has Been Suspended (Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpada).

Whatever nun, knowing that another nun is one who speaks thus, has not performed the *anudhamma* (corrective procedure), and has not relinquished that view, should eat together with her, live together with her, or share a sleeping place with her, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
Pācittiya 148: The Training Rule on Thorns.
If even a male novice (*samaṇuddesa*) should speak thus: [text continues]

“I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One in such a way that those things called ‘obstructive states’ by the Blessed One are not actually capable of being obstacles for one who indulges in them.
That novice nun should be addressed by the bhikkhunīs as follows:
“Do not say this, noble lady; do not misrepresent the Blessed One. It is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One, for the Blessed One would not speak in such a way.”
“Venerable lady, in many ways the Blessed One has stated that for a novice monk, certain things are obstructive conditions; they are sufficient to be an obstacle for one who indulges in them.
If, even when addressed thus by the bhikkhunīs, that novice monk should persist as before, then that novice monk should be told by the bhikkhunīs:
“From this day forward, venerable lady, you must no longer represent that Blessed One as your teacher.”
“Go away, perish!

If a nun, knowing that a novice has been thus expelled, should support him, or attend upon him, or eat together with him, or share a sleeping place with him, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 149: The Training Rule on Those in Accordance with the Dhamma.
If a nun, when being addressed by nuns in accordance with the Dhamma, should say:
"Venerable ladies, I will not train in this training rule until I have consulted another nun who is competent and a bearer of the Vinaya," she commits an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Monks, a training nun must learn, inquire about, and question [the rules]; this is the proper course therein.
Pācittiya 150: The Training Rule on Discouragement.
Whichever nun, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, should speak thus: ‘What is the use of these minor and lesser rules?’”
“‘The training rules that have been recited lead only to remorse, vexation, and anxiety,’ [if she says this], there is an offense of expiation for one who disparages the training rules.
Pācittiya 151. The Training Rule on Delusion:
“Whatever bhikkhunī, when the Pātimokkha is being recited every half-month, should speak thus:”
“Just now, noble lady, I have come to know that this rule, it seems, has been handed down in the Sutta, is included in the Sutta, and comes up for recitation every half-month.
If other bhikkhunīs should know that this bhikkhunī has previously sat through the recitation of the Pātimokkha two or three times,
let alone more than that, there is no release for that bhikkhunī on account of ignorance.
There is the case where she has committed an offense there, and she must be dealt with according to the rule; furthermore, delusion should be imposed upon her:
"It is a loss for you, noble lady, it is ill-gotten for you, that when the Pātimokkha was being recited, you did not pay close attention and apply your mind thoroughly.
This is the *pācittiya* offense regarding that deluding.
Pācittiya 152. The Training Rule on Striking.
Whatever nun, being angry and displeased with another nun, should give her a blow, there is an offense entailing expiation.
Pācittiya 153. The Training Rule on the Palm-Slap.
If a bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased with another bhikkhunī, should raise her hand (to strike), it is an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*).
*Pācittiya* 154: The Training Rule on Groundless Accusations.
If a bhikkhunī should groundlessly charge a bhikkhunī with an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), it is an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*).

Pācittiya 155. The Training Rule on Intentionally Causing Remorse Whichever bhikkhunī should intentionally cause remorse in a bhikkhunī, thinking, "In this way she will be uncomfortable even for a moment," making this alone the reason and no other, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Pācittiya 156. The Training Rule on Eavesdropping Whichever bhikkhunī should eavesdrop upon bhikkhunīs who are quarreling, disputing, or engaged in an argument, thinking, "I will listen to what they say," making this alone the reason and no other, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
