Whatever nun, however, should stand eavesdropping on nuns who have fallen into quarreling, brawling, or dispute, thinking, "I will hear what these women say," making this alone her motive and no other, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
The fifteenth section, the Section on Views (Diṭṭhivagga). The Section on What is Righteous (Dhammikavagga).
Pācittiya 157. The Training Rule on Obstructing Formal Acts:
Whichever bhikkhunī, having given her consent for formal acts that are in accordance with the Dhamma, subsequently falls into a state of reproach, incurs an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Pācittiya 158. The Training Rule on Going Without Giving Consent: [The rule concerning a bhikkhunī who goes to a formal act without having given her consent.]

If a nun, while a formal discussion for decision is being held in the Saṅgha, should rise from her seat and depart without having given her consent, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya). Pācittiya 159:

The Rule on the Weak If a nun, after a robe has been given by a unanimous Saṅgha, should later fall into a state of disparagement, saying, “The nuns are diverting the Saṅgha’s gains according to personal intimacy,” it is an offense entailing confession.
Pācittiya 160. The Training Rule on Diverting.
Whatever bhikkhunī, knowing that a gain intended for the Saṅgha has been diverted, should divert it to an individual person, there is an offense of expiation.
Pācittiya 161. The Training Rule on Valuables.
Whatever nun, however, should pick up or cause to be picked up a gem or what is considered a gem, except within a monastery or within a dwelling, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

Furthermore, having picked up or caused to be picked up a gem or what is considered a gem within a monastery or within a dwelling, it should be deposited by the nun with the thought: "He to whom it belongs shall take it away. This is the proper course in such a case.
Pācittiya 162: The Training Rule on the Needle Case.
Whatever nun should have a needle case made of bone, ivory, or horn, it is an offense entailing confession involving breaking [the object].
Pācittiya 163: The Training Rule on Beds and Chairs.

When a nun is having a new bed or chair made, it should be made with legs eight finger-breadths high according to the Sugata’s finger-breadth, excluding the lower crossbar. For one who exceeds that measurement, it is an offense entailing confession involving cutting down [the legs].
Pācittiya 164. The Training Rule on Cotton-Filling.
Whatever bhikkhunī should have a bed or a bench made stuffed with cotton, there is an offense of expiation involving tearing it out.
Pācittiya 165. The Training Rule on the Itch-Covering Cloth.
Now, when a nun is having an itch-covering cloth made, it must be made according to the proper measure. Herein, this is the measure:
four spans of the Sugata-span in length, and two spans across. For one who exceeds that, there is an offense entailing confession after the cutting down [of the excess].
Pācittiya 166: The Training Rule on Nanda Whatever nun should have a robe made the size of the Sugata’s robe, or larger, it is an offense entailing expiation with cutting down.
Herein, this is the measure of the Sugata’s robe for the Sugata: nine spans of the Sugata’s span in length, and six spans across; this is the measure of the Sugata’s robe for the Sugata.
The sixteenth chapter, on the Dhammika group.
Venerable ladies, the one hundred and sixty-six rules of expiation (pācittiya) have been recited.
Regarding this, I ask you, venerable ladies: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter? A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
You are pure in this matter, friends; therefore you are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The Pācittiya rules are concluded.
The Pāṭidesanīya rules:
Now, venerable ladies, these eight Pāṭidesanīya rules come up for recitation.
Pāṭidesanīya 1: The Training Rule on Requesting Ghee.
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request ghee and eat it, that nun must confess:
“Venerable ladies, I have fallen into a blameworthy, unbecoming, and confessable offense; I confess it.”
The Second Offense Requiring Confession: The Training Rule on Requesting Oil.
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request oil and consume it...
[as before] ...I confess that.
Pāṭidesanīya 3: The Training Rule on Requesting Honey.
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request honey and eat it … [as before] … I confess that.
Pāṭidesanīya 4. The Training Rule on Requesting Molasses:
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request molasses and eat it...
[as before] ...I confess that.
The Fifth Training Rule on Requesting Fish:
Whatever nun, not being ill, having requested fish, should eat it...
[as before] ...I confess that.
Pāṭidesanīya 6. The Training Rule on Requesting Meat:
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request meat and eat it...
[as before] ...I confess that.
The Seventh Training Rule on Requesting Milk (Pāṭidesanīya 7):
Whatever nun, not being ill, having requested milk, should eat it...
[as before] ...I confess that.
The Eighth Offense Requiring Confession: The Training Rule on Requesting Curd.
Whatever nun, not being ill, should request curd and eat it, that nun must confess:
"Venerable ladies, I have committed a blameworthy, unsuitable offense requiring confession; I confess it."
Venerable ladies, the eight rules on matters to be confessed have been recited.
Therefore, I ask the venerable ladies: Are you pure in this matter?
A second time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
A third time I ask: Are you pure in this matter?
The venerable ones are pure in this matter; therefore they are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The Pāṭidesanīya rules are concluded.
The Sekhiyas:
Now, venerable ladies, these Sekhiya rules come up for recitation.
The Chapter on Being Fully Circular.
Sekhiya 1. The Training Rule on the Circular Fold:
"I shall put on the lower robe circularly"—this training is to be observed.
Sekhiya 2. The Second Training Rule on the Circular Fold: [The same as above.]
"I shall put on my upper robe evenly all around"—this training is to be observed.
(Sekhiya 2) The Training Rule on Being Well-Covered:
"I shall go well-covered among the houses"—this training is to be observed. (Sekhiya 3)
Sekhiya 4. The Training Rule on Being Well-Covered:

"I shall sit well-covered in an inhabited area"—this training is to be observed. Sekhiya 5. The Training Rule on Being Well-Restrained: [I shall be well-restrained in an inhabited area—this training is to be observed.]
"I shall go well-restrained among the houses," this training is to be observed.
(Sekhiya 6) The second training rule on being well-restrained:
"I shall sit well-restrained among the houses," this training is to be observed.
Sekhiya 7. The Training Rule on Lowered Eyes:
"I will walk with lowered eyes in inhabited areas"—this training is to be observed.
Sekhiya 8. The Second Training Rule on Lowered Eyes: [The same rule as above.]

"‘I will not teach the Dhamma to one who is not ill with his head veiled’—this training is to be observed."

"I shall not teach the Dhamma to one whose head is veiled, unless they are ill"—this is the training to be observed.

Majority Decision.

Decision on the Basis of What is Worse.
